speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The first concerns whether the accounts of Government agencies are reliable and prepared in accordance with the law.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second involves checks on individual public agencies' compliance with rules and procedures, for example, the rules that guard against wastage of public funds and excess spending.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The first issue is whether the accounts of public agencies are proper and reliable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The same is true for the Statutory Boards, all of which received an unmodified audit opinion from their respective auditors for the financial year (FY) 2015/2016.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In other words, the accounts of the Ministries, Departments, Organs of State and Statutory Boards have all been found by independent auditors to be reliable and prepared in accordance with the law.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Public funds are properly accounted for and we know what they are being used for.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second type of AGO audit, as I mentioned, concerns the rules and procedures in individual public agencies, for example, those that aim at avoiding wastage.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Are the rules adequate and were the rules complied with?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As we review AGO's findings in this regard, there are three key questions we ask within the Government and which everyone should be concerned about.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, what is the scale of the shortcomings and do they reflect a systemic weakness in the Government?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, is there financial malfeasance, for example, fraud or corruption?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Third, how are Government agencies dealing with the lapses that are found so as to avoid the problems being repeated?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Most of the lapses were due to non-compliance by individual officers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In some cases, individual agencies had not followed full and thorough procedures in approving contracts or payments, as required in our internal rules.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The respective Ministries and agencies have, in all instances, taken steps to rectify the weaknesses identified.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It will be unrealistic to expect that there are no lapses found within the system each time a serious audit is done.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With over 140,000 officers in the Public Service handling hundreds of thousands of transactions each year, human laxity or errors of judgement will happen.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We take each and every lapse seriously, but if nothing was found by AGO, we would be very concerned about the independence and rigour of AGO's audits.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If there are any suspicions of wrongdoing, AGO does not hesitate to report them to the relevant authorities and highlight them in its report.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: From time to time, we do come across such instances.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have zero tolerance for fraud or corruption.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Everyone knows this: the Government acts promptly and thoroughly to investigate such cases.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Indeed, this zero tolerance has itself kept fraud and corruption in check.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is why we have a situation in Singapore that many countries seek to emulate.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Singapore has consistently been ranked by institutions, such as the World Bank and Transparency International, as amongst the least corrupt nations in the world, with the likes of Finland, Switzerland, Sweden and Denmark.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: How do Government agencies respond to AGO's observations?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Auditor-General has himself noted from our public agencies' responses that they take the AGO audit observations seriously, including putting in place measures to prevent future occurrence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Permanent Secretaries of each Ministry and the Chief Executives of the Statutory Boards are responsible for ensuring that the lapses are rectified and steps are taken to minimise recurrence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about actions taken on officers responsible for lapses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Where there is evidence of individual responsibility for the lapses, the officers responsible have been subjected to the appropriate disciplinary actions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One officer was put on a performance review process for repeated poor performance and subsequently, left the organisation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The first is contract management, particularly amongst agencies that do not manage construction projects regularly and, hence, may not have sufficient expertise and experience to robustly assess costs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The new Building and Infrastructure Centre of Excellence that we have set up under JTC this year will advise Government agencies which lack in-house expertise, and help us strengthen the public sector's capabilities in managing infrastructure projects.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Members may recall, this was an area that needed improvement, as highlighted by AGO a few years ago.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We took major steps to strengthen public sector procurement.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Since 2014, Permanent Secretaries and Chief Executives of agencies have been required to report to the Ministry of Finance regularly with an assessment of the findings in procurement audits and their follow-up actions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We published the Essentials of Procurement Handbook to ensure top management is apprised of procurement issues.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The procurement specialist track was launched in 2014 and we updated the accompanying training programmes to professionalise the procurement function.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We also instituted the Procurement Leaders Programme to groom procurement leaders to better guide and supervise their officers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is not perfect, but it is a system that has given Singapore international recognition for clean and efficient Government.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Senior Minister of State give us proper perspectives on this, to borrow the words of Ms Sylvia Lim?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is a world of difference between the lapses found in Government agencies and those of Aljunied-Hougang-Punggol East Town Council (AHPETC) or now known as AHTC.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They are different in scale, in nature and in the way Government agencies and the Town Council have each responded to problems when they are found.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Its own auditors repeatedly gave the Town Council a "Disclaimer of Opinion", which is the least desirable audit opinion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: AGO concluded in 2015 that there was "no assurance that AHPETC's accounts are accurate and reliable or that public funds are properly spent, accounted for and managed." There is no similar problem in the Government.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The accounts of Ministries, Departments, Organs of States and Statutory Boards have all been found by AGO and independent auditors to be reliable and prepared in accordance with the law.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Public funds are properly accounted for and we know what they are being used for.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, the problems at AHTC, formerly AHPETC, are of a systemic nature, not just a matter of individual lapses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To quote KPMG in their July 2016 report, "Control failures are pervasive, cutting across key areas of governance, financial 	Page: 17 control, financial reporting, procurement and records management over the course of five years …. there is an issue larger than the sum of individual lapses at AHTC".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As I explained earlier, there has been no such systemic problem in the Government.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: From this year's and past years' AGO reports, there is no evidence of widespread compliance problems.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Third, in the case of AHPETC, there are serious issues to do with personal gains from related third-party transactions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The general manager, deputy general manager and secretary of the Town Council were also the owners and directors of FM Solutions and Services Private Limited (FMSS) which provided managing agent services to AHPETC and received payments.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In addition, the secretary of AHPETC was a sole owner of FM Solutions and Integrated Services (FMSI) which provided maintenance and lift rescue services to AHPETC and, likewise, received payments.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In a review carried out by the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA), it was found that the profit margins of FMSS were abnormally high.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The conflicts of interest highlighted by AGO in the AHPETC case are fundamentally different from the case of Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP) and its subsidiary, NYP International (NYPi), that was highlighted in the AGO report.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As explained by Acting Minister for Education, Mr Ong Ye Kung yesterday, in the case of NYP and NYPi, there were no questions of personal gain.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There was no personal interest involved on the part of the directors of NYP and NYPi and no leakage of money to any third parties.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: NYPi is wholly owned by NYP and any profits made by NYPi will only benefit NYP.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Fourth, our Government agencies and AHPETC have been completely different in the way they responded to problems when they are found.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Notwithstanding the shortcomings and failures identified by their own auditors and, subsequently AGO, AHPETC did not take prompt measures to rectify these problems despite repeated requests by the Ministry of National Development (MND) to do so.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This resulted in MND having to bring an application to Court and it was only after the Court order was made that KPMG was appointed as an independent accountant by AHPETC.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: KPMG has been issuing monthly reports since April 2016.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the June 2016 KPMG report, AHTC has updated and implemented its revised conflict of interest policy which now extends to AHPETC's Town Councillors, management and employees, and supporting procedures to manage conflict of interest.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, the other remediation plans on the governance of related party transactions were still unresolved.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: By contrast, every Government agency takes AGO findings seriously.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Where there are lapses, they are openly acknowledged and steps taken to address them as soon as possible.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Auditor-General has himself noted their commitment to rectify the lapses and put in place measures to prevent future occurrences.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, to conclude, let me emphasise once again that the lapses found in the Government are wholly different from AHTC's problems.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is no systemic weakness in Government agencies, unlike what the auditors have found at the Town Council.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Unlike AHPETC, too, there was no question of personal gains in any of the lapses highlighted in this year's AGO report.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And finally, the Ministries and the agencies have, in all instances, taken steps to rectify the weaknesses identified.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our system is transparent, accountable 	Page: 18 and responsive and we look forward to the same in AHTC as it hopefully rectifies its problems.
